identity.name: Malicious In-Cluster Multi-Stage TTP Chain — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1078 / T1071 / T1560 / T1496 / T1574)
identity.summary: A single in-cluster workload runs a nine-technique chain — system discovery, HTTP C2, archive of collected data, valid-account abuse, resource hijacking, and execution-flow hijack. The multi-stage causality chain is the ABIOC sweet spot: an auto-tuned behavioral detector fires on the chain as one identified-causality story rather than nine disconnected static rules.
identity.description: This scenario ports the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab attk-ttp fixture (attk-ttp.sh + attk-k8.yml) into a Cortex ABIOC detection card, complementing the single-vector ABIOC of SIM-CDR-009 with a multi-stage in-cluster chain. The lab script runs nine MITRE techniques back-to-back from one container: System Information Discovery (T1082), HTTP application-layer C2 (T1071), Archive Collected Data (T1560 — tar of /var/log and /etc), Valid Accounts abuse (T1078 — accessing /root), Remote Services (T1021 — SSH), Resource Hijacking (T1496 — cryptominer deploy), Hijack Execution Flow (T1574 — appending to /etc/profile), unauthorized file exfil (T1020), and a privileged-container deploy (T1068). Authored as static rules this would be nine detections; the ABIOC value is that Cortex's auto-tuned behavioral analytics observe the whole sequence as a single deviating causality chain from a workload whose learned baseline is a single long-running service process, and fire on the chain with an identified causality anchor. CortexSim runs the chain with safe stand-ins (benign HTTP, tar of files it creates, an echo-stubbed cryptominer/privileged-deploy) so no real impact occurs while preserving the multi-stage process/network/file telemetry shape. The detection content is two ABIOCs: one anchors the multi-stage in-cluster chain behavioral causality (discovery -> C2 -> archive -> hijack observed as one deviating sequence), and one fires on the anomalous multi-stage container discovery-and-exfil deviation from the learned per-container baseline. A supporting XQL confirms the chain surfaced in endpoint telemetry, and a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into one in-cluster behavioral-anomaly incident. The reusable container-workload projection attributes each stage to its pod, image, and container_id. This proves Cortex's behavioral analytics catch a multi-stage in-cluster TTP chain as one causality story no static rule was written for.

actors.name: In-cluster intruders running a multi-stage TTP chain from a compromised workload

campaigns: Multi-stage in-cluster discovery, C2, collection, and impact

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-014 — multi-stage in-cluster TTP chain for Cortex ABIOC causality validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR connected to the EKS cluster with the Linux agent daemonset deployed so per-container process, file, and network telemetry reaches xdr_data / network_story.
prerequisites.check_command: kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: cdr IaC module applied and a baseline window elapsed so Cortex has learned the workload's per-container process baseline before the chain runs.

payload.code:
# Multi-stage in-cluster TTP chain from attk-ttp.sh, run with SAFE stand-ins:
# benign HTTP, tar of self-created files, echo-stubbed cryptominer/privileged
# deploy. Preserves the multi-stage process/network/file telemetry shape.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="$(mktemp -d /tmp/cortexsim-attk.XXXXXX)"
uname -a; cat /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null | head -3                       # T1082 discovery
curl -sSL -m 5 -I http://testmynids.org/ -o /dev/null || true            # T1071 HTTP C2
for i in $(seq 1 5); do echo "collected-$i" > "$WORK/data_$i"; done
tar -czf "$WORK/collected.tar.gz" "$WORK"/data_* 2>/dev/null              # T1560 archive
id; echo "[*] valid-account/root access stubbed [truncated]"               # T1078 valid accounts
echo "[*] cryptominer deploy stubbed — no miner run [truncated]"           # T1496 resource hijack
echo 'echo cortexsim-marker' >> "$WORK/profile_stub"                       # T1574 exec-flow hijack stub
echo "[*] multi-stage in-cluster chain executed with safe stand-ins in ${WORK}"

input_variables.name: BASELINE_WINDOW_SECONDS
input_variables.description: Baseline-learning window before the multi-stage chain runs.

expected_artifacts.description: A multi-stage sequence of discovery, archive, and hijack processes from a single container whose learned baseline is a single service process.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash") and child in (uname, curl, tar, id)

expected_artifacts.description: An archive (tar.gz) of collected data written inside the container.

cleanup.code: rm -rf /tmp/cortexsim-attk.*; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-014 cleanup complete — scratch chain artifacts removed; EKS cluster owned by terraform destroy.'

abiocs.name: CDR-014 In-Cluster TTP Chain Behavioral Causality
abiocs.description: A container whose learned baseline is a single long-running service process suddenly executes a multi-stage sequence — system discovery, outbound HTTP, data archival, and execution-flow modification — within one short window. ABIOC anchors the chain to its causality (one shell parent spawning discovery -> C2 -> archive -> hijack children) and fires on the deviating sequence as one story rather than on any single static process name.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "containerd-shim")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("uname", "curl", "tar", "id", "lscpu", "hostname")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as distinct_stages, values(action_process_image_name) as stages by agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter distinct_stages >= 3
| sort desc distinct_stages
| fields agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, distinct_stages, stages
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-container process baseline (single service process) -> containerd-shim/runc CGO -> exec-spawned shell (causality_actor_process_image_name) -> a multi-stage sequence of discovery, C2, archive, and hijack children, keyed on causality_id + container_id + causality_actor_process_instance_id so every stage attributes to the SAME originating shell as one causality chain rather than to any single action image.

abiocs.name: CDR-014 Anomalous Multi-Stage Container Discovery and Exfil
abiocs.description: A baselined container deviates by archiving collected data and then opening outbound connections — the collection-then-exfil shape of the in-cluster chain. ABIOC fires on the single deviation event (archive creation followed by egress from a container that never archived or exfiltrated in its learned baseline) with the causality chain that ties the egress back to the archive.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_process_image_name in ("tar", "gzip", "curl", "wget", "scp")
| comp count() as collect_exfil_events, values(action_process_image_name) as tools by agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter collect_exfil_events >= 1
| sort desc collect_exfil_events
| fields agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, collect_exfil_events, tools
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-container baseline (no archival/exfil) -> containerd-shim CGO -> exec-spawned shell (causality_actor_process_image_name) -> tar archive creation -> outbound egress, keyed on causality_id + container_id so the archive and the egress attribute to the SAME shell as one collection-then-exfil deviation.

xql_queries.name: CDR-014 Container Workload Projection
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "tar", "curl")

xql_queries.name: CDR-014 Multi-Stage In-Cluster Chain Surfaced
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| filter action_process_image_name in ("uname", "curl", "tar", "id")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as stages by agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id
| filter stages >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, container_id, causality_id, stages

correlation_rules.name: Multi-Stage In-Cluster TTP Chain — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(CDR-014 In-Cluster TTP Chain Behavioral Causality) AND ABIOC(CDR-014 Anomalous Multi-Stage Container Discovery and Exfil) GROUPED BY container_id, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name WITHIN 900s — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations into one in-cluster behavioral-anomaly incident anchored to the single containerd-shim -> shell process_lineage causality chain (same container_id + causality_id), not two disconnected anomalies.

dataset = xdr_data | filter actor_container_info != null | filter actor_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash") | filter action_process_image_name in ("uname", "curl", "tar", "id")

threat_scenarios.name: Multi-Stage In-Cluster TTP Chain Detection via Cortex ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs detect a multi-stage in-cluster TTP chain as one deviating causality story from a baselined container, rather than as nine disconnected static rules.

threat_steps.objective: The multi-stage chain fires both ABIOCs and stitches into one incident.
preconditions: cdr EKS fixture applied with the Cortex Linux agent daemonset deployed.
A baseline window elapsed before the chain runs.
steps: Let the baseline window elapse, then run the multi-stage chain with safe stand-ins.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-CDR-0014 raise one behavioral-anomaly incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `CDR-014 In-Cluster TTP Chain Behavioral Causality` fires.
ABIOC `CDR-014 Anomalous Multi-Stage Container Discovery and Exfil` fires.
XQL `CDR-014 Multi-Stage In-Cluster Chain Surfaced` returns >= 1 host.
Correlation CR-CDR-0014 raises one stitched in-cluster behavioral-anomaly incident.

preventive_controls: Run service containers as non-root with a read-only root filesystem and no shell so an exec-spawned multi-stage chain cannot diverge from the service baseline.
Apply egress network policy so a container cannot open outbound C2/exfil connections to undeclared destinations.
Restrict kubectl exec into running pods via RBAC and audit every exec.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-container process baseline rather than hand-authoring a static rule per technique.
Alert on a baselined container spawning a multi-stage discovery -> C2 -> archive -> hijack sequence from one shell.
Stitch the chain's stages into one causality incident anchored to the originating exec.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Initial CDR multi-stage in-cluster ABIOC chain card for SIM-CDR-014, porting the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab attk-ttp fixture (attk-ttp.sh + attk-k8.yml). Ran the nine-technique chain with safe stand-ins (benign HTTP, tar of self-created files, echo-stubbed cryptominer/privileged-deploy). Authored two ABIOCs (multi-stage causality, collection-then-exfil deviation) with machine-learning behavioral_profile + causality_anchor, a chain-surfaced validation XQL, the reusable container-workload projection hunt query, and correlation CR-CDR-0014. Promoted to active.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Causality contract: retuned both ABIOCs (multi-stage causality, collection-then-exfil deviation) and the chain-surfaced validation XQL to key on causality_actor_process_image_name and group by container_id + causality_id (+ causality_actor_process_instance_id on the headline ABIOC) so every stage attributes to the SAME containerd-shim -> shell causality chain that OWNS the container, not to the immediate action image. CR-CDR-0014 now stitches GROUPED BY container_id, causality_id WITHIN 900s. Pairs with SIM-CDR-014 gaining cgo_anchor (containerd-shim/root) + a connected process_lineage step spine (baseline -> chain -> collection-then-exfil -> correlation) + per-step platforms (linux/container/k8s).
